There are five size variants which can be used to add or remove emphasis: , (default), , , and . Use the attribute to control a button's size.

Use the slot to render an icon before the button's label. In addition, use the slot to render an icon after the button's label. While not required, the following example uses the component from to present icons using Material Symbols.

Use the attribute to control whether a button can be used for binary selection and the attribute to control the selected state. When clicked, a cancellable event is emitted followed by an and event. To cancel selection change, call during .

Use the attribute to control the behavior of a button. By default, is . You can change this to or to submit or reset a parenting form when clicked. When submitting a form, you can use the and attributes to specify a value.
Buttons can also behave like links by specifying a URL using the attribute. You can also specify , and similar to native anchor tags.

Buttons are density-aware and adjust their vertical spacing based on the and custom CSS properties. The default density size is 4dp. Buttons support negative density scales down to -3, with each step reducing the visual height by one density unit. Regardless of visual size, buttons maintain a 48x48dp minimum touch target to ensure reliable accessibility.
The following illustrates applying density to the and sized buttons.
<m3e-button variant="filled" size="extra-small" class="density-3"> <m3e-icon slot="icon" name="stars"></m3e-icon> Density -3 </m3e-button> <!-- Additional buttons omitted for brevity -->
.density-3 { --md-sys-density-scale: -3; } /* Additional classes omitted for brevity */
By default, buttons are given the ARIA role , indicating they are clickable elements that trigger actions.
Icons slots have to ensure icons are always hidden from assistive technologies.

When disabling using either the or attribute, is used to convey to assistive technologies that the button is disabled. If disabled using , is retained to convey that the button continues to be interactive.

When is specified, the ARIA role is used instead of to convey the button provides an interactive reference to a resource. In addition, the component presents an internal anchor, hidden from assistive technologies, used to invoke native browser features such a context menu options and tooltips.
For toggle buttons, is used to convey the selected state, even when disabled.
